title: WIDA Reading Mini-Practice: The Animal Shelter
overview: A short reading practice set built around one connected text about a community animal shelter. Students read each part, then answer a question that grows in difficulty: locate a detail, sequence events, infer, use vocabulary, and identify the main idea. Estimated time is about 15 minutes.

sections.title: Read and Answer: The Animal Shelter
sections.directions: Read each part of the article. Then answer the question for that part. Use only the text to answer.

items.title: Part 1: A New Shelter
passage: Last year, the town opened a new animal shelter on Oak Street.
The shelter takes in dogs and cats that have no home.
Volunteers feed the animals, clean the cages, and play with them every day.
The shelter's goal is to find a safe family for each animal.
items.prompt: Click the sentence that tells the shelter's goal.

sentences.text: Last year, the town opened a new animal shelter on Oak Street.
The shelter takes in dogs and cats that have no home.
Volunteers feed the animals, clean the cages, and play with them every day.
The shelter's goal is to find a safe family for each animal.

items.correct: Correct. The last sentence states the shelter's goal: to find a safe family for each animal.
items.support: Scan for the key word "goal." The answer is usually in the same sentence.

items.title: Part 2: What Volunteers Do
passage: Volunteers do many jobs at the shelter.
In the morning, they fill the food and water bowls.
They also walk the dogs and brush the cats.
They do not give the animals medicine; only the vet does that.
items.prompt: Which jobs do volunteers do? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Fill the food and water bowls

items.correct: Correct. Volunteers fill bowls, walk dogs, and brush cats. Only the vet gives medicine.
items.hint: One job is done by the vet, not the volunteers.
items.support: Check each choice against the text. Watch the sentence with "do not."

items.title: Part 3: Adoption Day
passage: First, a family visits the shelter to meet the animals.
Next, they choose a pet they would like to take home.
Then a volunteer helps them fill out the adoption papers.
Finally, the family takes their new pet home.
items.prompt: Put the steps of adopting a pet in the correct order.

items.text: A family visits the shelter to meet the animals.
They choose a pet to take home.
A volunteer helps them fill out the papers.
The family takes the new pet home.

items.correct: Correct. The order is visit, choose, fill out papers, then take the pet home.
items.hint: Use the order words: first, next, then, finally.
items.support: Order words signal each step in the process.

items.title: Part 4: A Word in Context
passage: The shelter is always grateful for donations.
People bring old towels, blankets, and bags of pet food.
These gifts help the shelter care for more animals each month.
items.prompt: In this passage, what does the word "donations" most likely mean?

options.text: gifts that people give to help

items.correct: Correct. People bring towels, blankets, and food as gifts, so donations are helpful gifts.
items.hint: Read the next sentence. What do people bring?
items.support: Context clues are the nearby words that explain a hard word.

items.title: Part 5: Finish the Summary
passage: The shelter opened last year and now helps many animals.
Thanks to volunteers and donations, more pets find homes each month.
The town is proud of its new shelter.
items.prompt: Complete the summary of the article.

segments.text: The new shelter helps animals find homes. With the help of volunteers and
, more pets are adopted each month. The town is

items.correct: Correct. Volunteers and donations help, and the town is proud of the shelter.
items.hint: Look back at the last part to see what people bring and how the town feels.
items.support: Match each blank to a detail you read in the article.

items.title: Part 6: The Big Idea
passage: From feeding animals to adoption day, the shelter works hard for its town.
Volunteers and donations keep it going.
Because of this care, many animals find a safe family.
items.prompt: What is the central idea of the whole article?

options.text: The shelter helps homeless animals find safe families.
Oak Street is the busiest street in town.
Cats are easier to care for than dogs.

items.correct: Yes. The whole article is about the shelter helping homeless animals find safe families.
items.hint: Think about what every part of the article was mostly about.
items.support: The central idea covers the whole text, not just one small detail.
